headline: High-risk filesystem and network interaction: gpt-engineer can write/run code in a shared project directory while rasa can expose outputs over chat channels, creating leakage and cascading-error risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: gpt-engineer writes files in a shared project directory and has no default self-isolation; rasa can ingest and emit conversational content over multiple chat surfaces. That creates a plausible instruction-smuggling path if gpt-engineer output is copied into rasa or shared via the project directory. The interaction is inferred, not directly documented, so uncertainty keeps this at medium.
conditions: IF gpt-engineer output is copied into rasa prompts or chat messages
IF both agents read from the same project directory or shared workspace
mitigations: Separate the project directory from any chat ingestion path
Add a manual review step before pasting code or logs into rasa
Prefix imported text as untrusted and strip instructions
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: gpt-engineer reads and writes the project directory and can call external models with broad egress; rasa handles text/voice and can send messages through third-party channels. If sensitive files land in the shared workspace, either agent can move them into outputs or API traffic. The pairwise leakage path is plausible from profiles alone, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF sensitive files are placed in the project directory
IF rasa forwards user text or attachments into external messaging APIs
mitigations: Keep secrets out of the shared project directory
Use a redaction pass before either agent processes files
Restrict rasa channels to non-sensitive test data

C_capability_conflict.rationale: gpt-engineer has broad filesystem write and subprocess execution in a per-project session, while rasa supports multiple external message channels and allowlisted egress. Even though rasa is not shown writing files, both can act on the same project artifacts or downstream resources, so overlapping mutable-resource control is plausible. Uncertainty about exact shared resources pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same project directory
IF rasa is configured to write artifacts or trigger downstream actions
mitigations: Serialize access with a simple operator checklist
Disable concurrent runs on the same workspace
requires-engineering: add file locks or orchestration locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: gpt-engineer produces code and files that can be treated as authoritative artifacts, while rasa is a dialogue system that can relay or act on text across chat channels. If rasa consumes gpt-engineer output without verification, errors can cascade into incorrect support responses or actions. The pathway is inferred rather than directly evidenced, so medium fits.
conditions: IF rasa uses gpt-engineer-generated text as source material
IF no human verification occurs before rasa relays the content
mitigations: Require human review of generated code before reuse
Add a verification checklist for any content passed to rasa

E_compliance.rationale: No explicit residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented for either agent. gpt-engineer touches generated source code and uses broad egress; rasa is a customer-support bot with text/voice channels, but the profiles do not show a concrete compliance conflict. Because the evidence is sparse, this remains low rather than none.
conditions: IF regulated data is routed through either agent
IF the deployment imposes residency or retention rules not shown in the profiles
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in both systems
Document data-class boundaries for each agent
